keys.explain.observed: {n} exposures of {target} were measured on detectors {detectors}, between {t0} and {t1}.
keys.explain.measured.variability: The target's flux was measured in every usable exposure by aperture photometry, and {n} wavelength-matched pairs were formed.
keys.explain.measured.motion: The target's position was measured against {refs} Gaia reference stars and averaged within each of {epochs} visits.
keys.explain.measured.quality: Each of {n} exposures was checked for usability before anything was measured.
keys.explain.method: Methods, in the order they ran: {methods}.
keys.explain.compared.variability: Only exposures at the same wavelength on the same detector were compared ({n} pairs); each difference was divided by its uncertainty after calibration against reference stars.
keys.explain.compared.motion: Positions were compared across {baseline} years with a straight-line motion model.
keys.explain.compared.quality: Usable and unusable exposures were counted by fixed rules.
keys.explain.result: The rule-based outcome is “{category}”. The statement recorded by the engine follows unchanged.
keys.explain.certainty: How certain: the thresholds, sensitivities and criteria behind the outcome are listed as recorded. None of them is a probability.
keys.explain.alternatives: {n} explanations were tested by stated rules; each status is listed as recorded.
keys.explain.limits: What this does not mean: a candidate is not a discovery, and an absence is bounded by the stated sensitivity. The recorded limitations follow.
